newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Liberals say no EU home for Turkey, Russia.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Liberals say no EU home for Turkey, Russia.

text.p: Turkey, Russia and Ukraine should not be allowed to join the European Union because they do not fit the traditional profile of the 15-member western bloc, the leader of a mainstream Dutch political party said on Saturday.

"The EU should only offer a place to those countries that share in the great formative events that shaped European history," Frits Bolkestein, outspoken chief of the conservative Liberal Party, told a meeting of party faithful in the central Dutch town of Ede.

The Liberal Party, currently the most popular political group in the Netherlands with a general election due in May of next year, is one of three in the right-left ruling coalition, but Bolkestein has opted to lead it from the parliamentary ranks rather than from within cabinet.

He said on Saturday that these three potential candidates for EU membership were too far removed from the bloc's historical traditions -- feudalism, the Renaissance, the Age of Reason and the development of democracy.
"Countries like the Ukraine, Russia and Turkey fall outside that. (EU) membership for these states would mean an end for the Union," he said.
The Netherlands holds the rotating EU presidency until June 30.
In February, Bolkestein wrote in Dutch daily newspaper de Volkskrant that Turkey was too poor and its culture and religion too different to that in the rest of the European Union.

Leaders of the bloc's Christian Democrat governments, including German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, later appeared to endorse these views, casting doubt on Ankara's long-standing application for EU membership.
But EU foreign ministers at a meeting in the Dutch town of Apeldoorn last month signalled that Turkey could one day join the western club.
Ukraine has recently improved its ties with the EU and last month Russian President Boris Yeltsin said he was interested in joining the bloc.
